note: validatePetition(d) returns only { readinessClass, propertyRegime, earliestDecreeDate, stateRuleKnown } with no flags, so this is a SPLIT engine: the oracle pins detectFlaggedIssues(state) as expected.flaggedIssues with flagsArgs ["state"], mirroring form-app.js's detectFlaggedIssues(state). Classification is first-match: not-yet-eligible (state or county residency short, separation short, decree before the waiting period), then incomplete (core details, custody plan or child-support worksheet, unavailable fault ground, uncontested without agreement, decree without service), else ready-to-file. All dates come from the persona state, so no clock is read.

personas.name: Ready to file: Illinois uncontested, no children, served by acceptance
personas.description: Both spouses agree; 14 months in Illinois (90 days needed), settlement agreement signed, financial disclosure ready, respondent signed an acceptance of service a week after filing, no children, no decree yet. Illinois has no waiting period before the decree. Expect readinessClass 'ready-to-file', property regime equitable, and no flags.

personas.name: Ready to file: California uncontested with children, waiting period pending
personas.description: California uncontested no-fault with two minor children, custody plan and guideline worksheet done ($1,240 a month), 9 months in state and 5 months in county, served personally on 2026-07-20. Expect 'ready-to-file', community property, earliest decree 2027-01-21 (six months and a day from service) and only the low waiting-period-pending flag.

flaggedIssues.description: California has a waiting period; the earliest date a decree may be entered is 2027-01-21.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Do not schedule the final hearing or submit the decree before that date.

personas.name: Not yet eligible: Texas residency and county residency short
personas.description: Texas petition filed after only 4 months in the state and 60 days in the county (6 months and 90 days are required). Everything else is complete. Expect 'not-yet-eligible' with high state-residency and county-residency flags and the low waiting-period flag (60 days from filing).

flaggedIssues.description: The petitioner has lived in Texas for 4 month(s); 6 month(s) are required before filing (Tex. Fam. Code 6.301 (6 months state, 90 days county), 6.702 (60 days from filing)).
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Wait until the residency period is met, or file in a state where a spouse already meets it.

flaggedIssues.description: The petitioner has lived in the county for 60 day(s); 90 days are required in Texas.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Wait until the county residency period is met, or file in the county where it is met.

flaggedIssues.description: Texas has a waiting period; the earliest date a decree may be entered is 2026-10-09.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Do not schedule the final hearing or submit the decree before that date.

personas.name: Not yet eligible: Pennsylvania contested no-fault, separation too short
personas.description: Contested Pennsylvania no-fault petition under 3301(d); the spouses separated 2026-03-01 and the petition is filed 2026-08-15, about 167 days against the one year required. Expect 'not-yet-eligible' with the high separation flag, and the low waiting-period flag (90 days from service).

flaggedIssues.description: A contested no-fault divorce in Pennsylvania needs 365 days of separation before filing, and the stated separation date is too recent.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Wait until the separation period has run, obtain the respondent's written agreement where the state allows, or plead an available fault ground.

flaggedIssues.description: Pennsylvania has a waiting period; the earliest date a decree may be entered is 2026-11-23.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Do not schedule the final hearing or submit the decree before that date.

personas.name: Incomplete: Florida with a fault ground, missing names and children paperwork
personas.description: Florida has no fault grounds (only irretrievable breakdown), yet adultery is pleaded; the respondent and marriage date are missing; there are children with no custody plan or child-support worksheet; no financial disclosure. Expect 'incomplete' with core-missing, ground-not-available, custody-plan, child-support and financial-disclosure flags.

flaggedIssues.description: Required petition details are missing: respondent name, marriage date.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Complete every required item before filing.

flaggedIssues.description: Florida has no fault grounds for divorce; only a no-fault ground (irretrievable breakdown or irreconcilable differences) can be pleaded.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Plead the state's no-fault ground instead of a fault ground.

flaggedIssues.description: There are minor children but no custody and parenting-time plan is documented.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Prepare a parenting plan (legal and physical custody, parenting time, decision-making) to file with the petition.

flaggedIssues.description: There are minor children but the state child-support guideline worksheet is not completed.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Complete the state guideline worksheet from both parents' incomes and parenting time, and record the monthly amount.

flaggedIssues.description: The financial disclosure or affidavit is not filed or ready. Most states require sworn disclosure of income, assets and debts.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Complete the state financial affidavit or disclosure form and exchange it with the other spouse.

flaggedIssues.description: The respondent has not yet been served. Service of process follows filing.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: After filing, serve the respondent personally, by acceptance of service, or by another method the court allows, and file proof of service.

flaggedIssues.description: Florida has a waiting period; the earliest date a decree may be entered is 2026-09-09.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Do not schedule the final hearing or submit the decree before that date.

personas.name: Not yet eligible: Washington decree entered before the 90-day waiting period
personas.description: Washington petition filed 2026-07-01, served 2026-07-10, but a decree is recorded as entered 2026-08-20; the 90 days run from the later of filing or service, so the earliest decree date is 2026-10-08. Name restoration is requested without a name and no divorce certificate is requested. Expect 'not-yet-eligible' with decree-before-waiting-period, name-restoration and certificate flags.

flaggedIssues.description: The decree date 2026-08-20 is before the earliest permitted date 2026-10-08 under the Washington waiting period.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Check the decree and waiting-period dates; a decree entered early may be void or voidable.

flaggedIssues.description: Restoration of a former name is requested, but the name to restore is not stated.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: State the exact former name to be restored in the petition and decree.

flaggedIssues.description: The decree is entered but no vital-records divorce certificate or certified decree is requested.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Order certified copies from the clerk, and a divorce certificate from the state vital-records office if needed (for example for a name change or remarriage).

personas.name: Ready to file with flags: unknown state, UCCJEA gap, military respondent, publication
personas.description: Minnesota is not in the verified rule table, so the default 90-day domicile rule applies and a verify-state-rule flag is raised. The children have lived there only 4 months (UCCJEA six-month home-state test), the respondent is on active duty and has not appeared, service is by publication, and no financial disclosure is ready. Expect 'ready-to-file' with unknown-state, home-state, military, publication and disclosure flags.

flaggedIssues.description: The children have lived in MN for 4 month(s). Under the UCCJEA a state is the home state for custody only after six consecutive months, so the court may lack custody jurisdiction.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Confirm which state is the children's home state before asking this court to decide custody.

flaggedIssues.description: "MN" is not in this tool's verified state-rule table, so the default 90-day domicile rule was used.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Verify the residency, waiting-period and property rules with the state court website or an attorney before relying on this result.

flaggedIssues.description: The financial disclosure or affidavit is not filed or ready. Most states require sworn disclosure of income, assets and debts.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Complete the state financial affidavit or disclosure form and exchange it with the other spouse.

flaggedIssues.description: The respondent is on active military duty and has not appeared. The Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (50 U.S.C. 3931) requires an affidavit before a default judgment.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: File the SCRA affidavit (check the DMDC database) before requesting a default decree.

flaggedIssues.description: Service by publication is a last resort and normally needs a court order and proof of a diligent search for the respondent.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: File a motion for alternate service with a declaration of diligent search before publishing.

personas.name: Ready to file with flag: New York with the shortened residency and a property mismatch
personas.description: New York needs two years of residency, or one year when the spouses married or lived as spouses in New York; this petitioner has 14 months and married in New York, so residency is met. The petition pleads community property although New York uses equitable distribution. A decree is entered with a certificate requested. Expect 'ready-to-file' with the property-approach-mismatch flag only.

flaggedIssues.description: The petition pleads community property division, but New York is a equitable state.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Plead the equitable approach used in New York.

personas.name: Incomplete: Ohio contested no-fault with no separation date
personas.description: Ohio contested no-fault needs a year of separation (ORC 3105.01(J)) but no separation date is recorded; 7 months in Ohio and 120 days in the county satisfy residency. Expect 'incomplete' with core-missing and separation-period (medium) flags.

flaggedIssues.description: Required petition details are missing: separation date.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Complete every required item before filing.

flaggedIssues.description: Ohio requires 365 days of separation for a contested no-fault divorce, but no separation date is recorded.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Record the date the spouses began living separate and apart.

personas.name: Incomplete: blank petition
personas.description: A fresh blank petition. Expect 'incomplete', with core-missing, financial-disclosure and not-yet-served flags.

flaggedIssues.description: Required petition details are missing: filing state, county, filing date, uncontested or contested, ground type, petitioner name, respondent name, marriage date, petitioner residency, minor children answer.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Complete every required item before filing.

flaggedIssues.description: The financial disclosure or affidavit is not filed or ready. Most states require sworn disclosure of income, assets and debts.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Complete the state financial affidavit or disclosure form and exchange it with the other spouse.

flaggedIssues.description: The respondent has not yet been served. Service of process follows filing.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: After filing, serve the respondent personally, by acceptance of service, or by another method the court allows, and file proof of service.
